Graduate Researcher · Biochemistry

MD Hamed Hasan

Caenorhabditis elegans/ Drug discovery/ Bioinformatics/ RNA-seq

I use the nematode C. elegans as a whole-animal model to screen Bangladeshi and Canadian plant extracts for anthelmintic activity — work that runs from culturing and synchronizing worms at the bench through to differential expression analysis at the terminal. Currently reading for an MSc in Biochemistry at Chattogram Veterinary and Animal Sciences University, supported by NST and UGC research fellowships.

About

My research sits deliberately across the wet lab and the dry lab. On the bench I maintain C. elegans and OP50 cultures, run L1 synchronization by bleaching, prepare solvent extracts of plant material, and carry out the assay chemistry that turns a crude extract into a testable compound. At the terminal I take the resulting data through RNA-seq and differential expression workflows, molecular docking, and statistical analysis in R.

That combination is the thread through most of what I do. My MSc thesis screens plant extracts against C. elegans and Haemonchus contortus for anthelmintic drug discovery. Alongside it I contribute to computational work on natural-compound screening and antiviral target identification, and I have co-authored two peer-reviewed papers applying machine learning to research literacy and researcher mental health.

I completed my BSc in Biochemistry & Molecular Biology at Gopalganj Science & Technology University in 2024, and I have been tutoring science students since 2017 — teaching remains a part of the work I care about.
